standard_prerequisites: filtration of a modal model through a set of formulas Gamma
the equivalence relation of agreeing on all formulas in Gamma
core_obligations: Prove that if Gamma is finite then any filtration M* of M through Gamma is finite, with a bound of 2^n on the size of W* when Gamma has n sentences
proof_roadmap: The worlds W* of the filtration are the equivalence classes of the agreement relation
Each class [w] is determined by the subset of Gamma true at its worlds: worlds in the same class agree on all of Gamma
Different classes determine different subsets, since agreement on all of Gamma is exactly the equivalence relation, so the map from W* to the powerset of Gamma is injective
Hence the cardinality of W* is at most that of the powerset of Gamma, i.e. at most 2^n for n sentences
difficulty_reason: A short injective-counting argument; formally H1, but the filtration setup must be recalled, hence H2.
